column3: Sits right before a verb to make a mild, friendly suggestion: 你不妨试试 is "why not give it a try". It suggests an easy option, not an order.
column6: Nǐ bùfáng xiān wènwen lǎoshī.
column7: You might as well ask the teacher first.

column3: Usually followed by 于 and a habit or pastime, and it carries disapproval: 沉迷于游戏, 手机 or 赌博. For something you simply love, use 着迷 or 喜欢.
column6: Tā chénmí yú wǎngluò yóuxì.
column7: He is addicted to online games.

column3: It is the everyday word for the archery bow, and 弓箭 is the usual pair "bow and arrow". The bow of a violin is 弓 too.
column4: 他拉开弓,射出了一支箭。
column5: 他拉開弓,射出了一支箭。
column6: Tā lākāi gōng, shèchū le yī zhī jiàn.
column7: He drew the bow and shot an arrow.

column3: Typically the head servant of a wealthy household, as in period dramas and novels. 管家婆 is the teasing name for a woman who holds the household purse strings.
column4: 管家把客人带到了客厅。
column5: 管家把客人帶到了客廳。
column6: Guǎnjiā bǎ kèrén dài dào le kètīng.
column7: The butler showed the guests to the living room.

column3: A noun for a social or cultural taboo, often with 犯 (to break one) or in 禁忌话题 "taboo subject". In medicine it also lists what a patient must avoid.
column4: 在这里,死亡是一个禁忌话题。
column5: 在這裡,死亡是一個禁忌話題。
column6: Zài zhèlǐ, sǐwáng shì yī gè jìnjì huàtí.
column7: Here, death is a taboo subject.

column3: Mostly heard in 胃口很好, 没胃口 and 胃口大. It also means taste or liking in general (这个工作不合我的胃口), and 倒胃口 means something puts you off. The character 胃 began as a picture of a stomach with food inside.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān méiyǒu wèikǒu.
column7: I have no appetite today.

column3: A set phrase of good wishes, written on cards and said at New Year or birthdays, usually after 祝你 or 祝您. It is not used to describe what happened to someone.
column4: 祝你新年快乐,心想事成!
column5: 祝你新年快樂,心想事成!
column6: Zhù nǐ xīnnián kuàilè, xīnxiǎngshìchéng!
column7: Happy New Year, and may all your wishes come true!

column3: A formal, positive word that mostly describes history, culture or tradition, as in 历史悠久. It is for spans of history and tradition, not everyday lengths: for a long wait or a long road, say 很久 or 很长.
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì lìshǐ yōujiǔ.
column7: This city has a long history.

column3: On its own it mostly means vegetarian food or plain: 吃素 (eat vegetarian), 素菜 (a vegetarian dish). Otherwise it is a building block in words such as 元素 and 因素. It is a picture of hands 廾 braiding thread 糸, and in today's form the top looks like 生 without the diagonal stroke.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān chī sù.
column7: I am eating vegetarian today.

column3: Seen on forms as 备注, the remarks box, and in 注解, a note explaining a text.
column4: 这一页的下面有一个注。
column5: 這一頁的下面有一個註。
column6: Zhè yī yè de xiàmiàn yǒu yī gè zhù.
column7: There is a note at the bottom of this page.

column3: Today it mostly means mysterious or deep, as in 玄妙 and 玄学; in speech 太玄了 says that something is too far-fetched to believe. It was the oldest basic color word for black, later replaced by 黑.
column4: 这件事说得太玄了，我不信。
column5: 這件事說得太玄了，我不信。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì shuō de tài xuán le, wǒ bù xìn.
column7: That story is too far-fetched, I don't believe it.

column3: It mostly turns up in compounds such as 瓦片 (a single tile) and 瓦房 (a house with a tile roof), and tiles are counted with 片: 一片瓦. It is a picture of fired pottery or a tile.
column6: Wūdǐng shàng pūzhe hóng wǎ.
column7: Red tiles cover the roof.

column3: You go somewhere to do it: 去海边度假. For a day off given by school or work, the word is 放假, and the holiday itself is 假期. Here 假 is read jià, for vacation; when it means fake or to borrow it is read jiǎ.
column4: 暑假我们打算去海边度假。
column5: 暑假我們打算去海邊度假。
column6: Shǔjià wǒmen dǎsuàn qù hǎibiān dùjià.
column7: This summer vacation we plan to go to the seaside for a holiday.

column3: You meet it in animal names like 梅花鹿 and 驯鹿, and in 鹿肉 for venison. The set phrase 指鹿为马, calling a deer a horse, means to twist the truth on purpose.
column6: Nà zhī lù pǎo jìn le shù lín.
column7: That deer ran into the woods.

column3: Any card of paper or plastic: a flash card, a birthday card, a collectible card. A bank card or SIM card is usually just 卡.
column6: Wǒ zuò le hěn duō shēngcí kǎpiàn.
column7: I made a lot of vocabulary cards.

column3: It stresses someone with no connection to you: 當作路人 means to treat as a stranger. 路人甲 is the nameless extra in a play or film, also used jokingly for any nobody.
column4: 路人都停下来看这只小狗。
column5: 路人都停下來看這隻小狗。
column6: Lùrén dōu tíng xiàlái kàn zhè zhī xiǎo gǒu.
column7: The passers-by all stopped to look at the puppy.

column3: A number plus 人次 counts visits, not different people: one person who comes three times adds three. It turns up in statistics for museums, hospitals, airports and tourism.
column4: 这个博物馆每年有两百万人次参观。
column5: 這個博物館每年有兩百萬人次參觀。
column6: Zhè ge bówùguǎn měi nián yǒu liǎng bǎi wàn réncì cānguān.
column7: This museum gets two million visits a year.

column3: Something personal that others should not pry into; its opposite is 公事, official business. Typical lines are 这是我的私事 and 上班时间不要办私事.
column4: 这是我的私事，你不用管。
column5: 這是我的私事，你不用管。
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de sīshì, nǐ bù yòng guǎn.
column7: This is my own business, you need not worry about it.

column3: The opposite of 具體 (concrete); used for ideas, explanations and art, as in 抽象畫, and 太抽象了 means it is too hard to grasp.
column4: 这个概念太抽象了,你能举个例子吗?
column5: 這個概念太抽象了,你能舉個例子嗎?
column6: Zhège gàiniàn tài chōuxiàng le, nǐ néng jǔ ge lìzi ma?
column7: This idea is too abstract. Can you give an example?

column3: You 回味 a good meal, a film or the old days by going over it again in your mind afterward; as a noun it is the aftertaste. Often 值得回味 or 回味无穷.
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng zhíde huíwèi.
column7: This film is worth mulling over.

column3: Describes a person's character: honest and upright, doing right even when it costs something. It praises people, not lines; a straight line is 直.
column6: Tā shì yī gè zhèngzhí de rén.
column7: He is an honest, upright person.

column3: It is the empty lot between buildings, or open ground left unbuilt: 空地 for children to play on, for parking, or for a market.
column6: Háizimen zài kòngdì shàng tī qiú.
column7: The children are kicking a ball on the empty lot.

column3: On its own it is the element in chemistry; in daily life it mostly turns up in compounds such as 二氧化碳 (carbon dioxide), 碳排放 (carbon emissions) and 低碳 (low-carbon).
column6: Méi zhǔyào yóu tàn zǔchéng.
column7: Coal is made mainly of carbon.

column3: Used of something in short supply, such as food, water, staff or money, and common in news and economic writing: 人手短缺 is a shortage of staff.
column4: 因为天气不好，蔬菜供应短缺。
column5: 因為天氣不好，蔬菜供應短缺。
column6: Yīnwèi tiānqì bù hǎo, shūcài gōngyìng duǎnquē.
column7: Because of the bad weather, the vegetable supply is short.

column3: The journey as a stretch from start to finish, often with a figurative sense: 人生旅程 is the journey of life. To say that you go on a trip, use 旅行.
column6: Zhè tàng lǚchéng huā le sān tiān.
column7: This journey took three days.

column3: A small cloth carried in a pocket for wiping the face or hands; a paper tissue is 纸巾 on the mainland and 面纸 in Taiwan.
column4: 他从口袋里拿出一条手帕。
column5: 他從口袋裡拿出一條手帕。
column6: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ ná chū yī tiáo shǒupà.
column7: He took a handkerchief out of his pocket.

column3: Mostly a wedding, but also any happy family event such as a birth. You hold it as 辦喜事, and 有喜事 means something is to be celebrated.
column6: Tāmen jiā zuìjìn yǒu xǐshì.
column7: Something happy is going on at their house lately.

column3: The everyday word for sesame seeds, as on bread or in 芝麻油. It also stands for something tiny, as in 芝麻小事, a trivial matter.
column6: Miànbāo shàng sǎ le yīxiē zhīma.
column7: Some sesame seeds were sprinkled on the bread.
